question: What is the main biological goal of puberty during adolescence?

options.B: Rapid increase in bone mineral density only
options.C: Attaining sexual maturity and reproductive capacity

explanation: You got this! Puberty is simply the body's natural transition to reach sexual maturity and the ability to reproduce. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is it helpful to know that puberty starts at different ages for different teenagers?

options.A: To avoid mistaking normal developmental variations for health problems
options.B: To accurately predict the exact adult height of every patient
options.C: To prevent teenagers from experiencing any emotional stress
options.D: To prescribe hormone therapy before puberty starts

explanation: Well done! Everyone’s body clock is unique. Knowing this helps us avoid unnecessary panic over what is actually totally normal growth. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which brain structure kicks off the hormonal changes of puberty?
explanation: Spot on! The hypothalamus is the master control center that starts the whole process by releasing puberty hormones. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h2)

question: What do luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) directly do to the gonads?

options.A: Stopping the secretion of growth hormone during sleep
options.B: Shutting down the pituitary gland through negative feedback
options.C: Stimulating the production of sex steroids like estrogen and testosterone
options.D: Directly causing the closure of the epiphyseal plates in long bones

explanation: Great job! LH and FSH act like messengers to the ovaries and testes, telling them to start producing sex hormones. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is usually the very first physical sign of puberty in girls?

options.A: Onset of the first menstrual period

explanation: Correct! The appearance of breast buds is typically the first visible sign that female puberty has kicked off. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why are menstrual cycles often irregular during the first year or two after a girl's first period?

options.A: The thyroid gland temporarily stops working during adolescence
options.B: The uterus is still too small to hold a normal volume of blood
options.C: The cycles are frequently anovulatory as the endocrine system matures
options.D: Girls consume too much dietary iron during their growth spurts

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! Because ovulation doesn't happen every single month right away, it takes time for the hormonal system to settle into a steady rhythm. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the earliest physical sign of puberty in boys?
explanation: Spot on! Testicular growth is the very first clinical sign that male puberty has begun. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why does a teenage boy's voice crack and deepen?

options.A: Hypertrophy of the salivary glands from increased testosterone
options.B: Narrowing of the pharynx due to rapid facial bone growth
options.C: Elongation of the vocal cords due to laryngeal cartilage growth
options.D: Swelling of the tonsils caused by an upper respiratory infection

explanation: Well done! Testosterone makes the voice box (larynx) grow larger, stretching the vocal cords and dropping the pitch of the voice. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h4)

question: According to Piaget, which stage of thinking do teenagers enter?
explanation: Correct! Teens enter the formal operational stage, where they start mastering abstract thinking and complex problem-solving. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why are teenagers more likely to take risks than adults?

options.A: The emotional limbic system matures faster than the impulse-controlling prefrontal cortex
options.B: The brain stops producing neurotransmitters entirely during puberty
options.C: The adolescent brain requires less sleep than the adult brain
options.D: Synaptic pruning causes a temporary loss of all memory function

explanation: You got it! The brain's emotional center develops faster than the part that controls impulses, making teens more prone to seeking thrills. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h5)

question: According to Erik Erikson, what is the main psychological challenge teenagers face?
explanation: Spot on! Teens are constantly figuring out the big question: 'Who am I and where do I fit in?' This is identity versus role confusion. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the main role of peer groups during the teenage years?

options.A: Replacing the need for any guidance from healthcare professionals
options.B: Providing a testing ground for independence and social identity away from parents
options.C: Accelerating the physical closure of growth plates in bones
options.D: Eliminating all internal body image anxiety and self-doubt

explanation: Great job! Friends give teenagers a safe space to practice being independent and figure out who they are outside of their families. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why do adolescent girls need extra iron in their diet?

options.B: To compensate for menstrual blood loss
options.C: To accelerate the growth of facial hair
options.D: To prevent the softening of tooth enamel

explanation: Correct! Because of monthly periods, girls lose some iron and need a good diet to keep their blood healthy and prevent anemia. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is a major reason eating disorders often start during the teenage years?

options.A: The permanent loss of taste buds during puberty
options.B: Intense body image concerns combined with rapid physical changes
options.C: Excessive physical exercise required by school curriculums
options.D: A complete lack of appetite caused by hormonal stabilization

explanation: You're doing great! Rapid body changes can make teens super self-conscious, sometimes triggering unhealthy eating habits. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of the HEEADSSS tool when assessing a teenager?

options.A: To systematically screen for lifestyle risk factors and psychosocial health
options.B: To diagnose underlying genetic disorders of the endocrine system
options.C: To calculate the exact caloric requirements for daily exercise
options.D: To determine the precise biological stage of puberty

explanation: Spot on! HEEADSSS is a helpful checklist nurses use to review a teen's home life, school, mental health, and safety. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h8)

question: Why should a nurse spend some time talking to a teenage patient alone during a health checkup?

options.A: To legally remove parental consent for all future medical treatments
options.B: To prevent the parents from hearing about routine vaccination schedules
options.C: To encourage honest discussion about sensitive topics like sex and substance use
options.D: To test whether the adolescent can survive without adult supervision

explanation: Brilliant! Privacy helps teenagers feel safe enough to open up about sensitive health topics they might hide in front of their parents. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h8)
